doc.title: Lou Marini interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 15, 2023

title: Inner sax parts and good arranging
summary: Fourth tenor and second alto parts are not easier; good writers like Phil Kelly cross parts for voice leading.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And there’s this myth I think that the fourth tenor and the second alto parts are easier. And often times they’re not because you get those, you fill in the harmonies and sometimes they’re a challenge to play and also you’re trying to fit in in the ensemble.

Well that’s one thing about good arrangers who actually take the time to, you know like sometimes the second tenor and the fourth tenor cross parts, just for voice leading, just so that you don’t have to play two repeated notes. So all of the sudden the fourth tenor is above the second tenor instead of being below it. But good writers are conscious of that. One of the best at that to me is the guy — Phil Kelly — who I started playing with him in Dallas. He was a drummer, great drummer too. But his charts, no matter what saxophone
part you are playing you feel like you’re playing the melody. And that’s — I try to do that in my parts. I don’t always succeed but I think about it you know.
